fatal_errors: The proposed W-Mo-Ta-Nb refractory high-entropy-alloy system does not reconstruct the CoCrFeNiMox-Ni/MoS2-Ag-Cr2O3 composite.
It omits the varied Mo content, spark-plasma-sintered composite architecture, sigma-phase strengthening, and temperature-dependent MoS2/Ag and oxide/silver-molybdate lubrication mechanisms.
The stated 500-1000 °C boundary excludes room-to-intermediate-temperature behavior and exceeds the target's validated upper limit of 800 °C.
The claimed 20% performance improvement and 15% falsification threshold are unsupported by the cited evidence.

The cited papers support the elevated-temperature mechanical properties of refractory HEAs but do not establish self-lubrication, friction reduction, wear resistance, or compatibility with the proposed lubricant phases.
explanation: The hypothesis recognizes the broad design principle of combining a strong high-temperature matrix with solid lubricants, but it remains generic and identifies the wrong material family. It provides no specific lubricant chemistry, processing route, microstructural mediator, or temperature-dependent tribofilm mechanism. Its baseline is undefined, its quantitative prediction is invented, and its proposed test lacks specified counterface, atmosphere, load, speed, and distance. The available evidence only supports RHEAs as strong, thermally stable matrices and therefore cannot validate the central tribological claim.
